title: Literate Programming in the Large
summary: Timothy Daly, an original author of the Axiom computer algebra system, talks about turning a large Common Lisp codebase into a literate program. He argues code should be written as readable manuals, and the talk was given at Write the Docs 2013.
why: HN recommends it in literate programming threads as a rare look at applying the idea to a huge, complex codebase, though some find it meandering.

quote.text: well worth watching: it talks about real, huge comolex systems, and how lp can help bring them back under control
